doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sonny Cohn and Al Aarons join the trumpet section
summary: Young recalls Sonny Cohn replacing Wendell Culley, who walked off after Marshal Royal's outburst, and Al Aarons arriving.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: And you talk about Al Aarons.
Who?
Al Aarons, the other trumpet player? The trumpet player was you…
Al Aarons?
Yeah, you, Thad Jones, Al Aarons, and Sonny Cohn.

Sonny Cohn. Well, I remember when Sonny Cohn came to the band and I remember when Al Aarons come to the band. Who did Sonny Cohn? Oh, that‘s when the trumpet player that, what‘s his name said something to and he got off and left.
Oh, right, you said that Marshall Royal said something to him and he got off and left.
[laughs] I don‘t know if you should put that on tape.
[laughs]
But he did that.
Yeah, we talked about it.
Yeah, we talked about that. What was his name?
I talked about Al Aarons and Sonny Cohn. Sonny Cohn.
Yeah, but I was saying, when Sonny Cohn came to the band I was telling you who he replaced.
Do you remember who that was?
I just got through talking about him. We just, that Marshall said.
Right, yeah, I don‘t remember.
That old man was so good. That old man, what‘s his name? He played ―Little Darling‖? Wendell Culley.
Wendell Culley, Wendell Culley.
Wendell Culley.
Right, so, Sonny took his place?

Yeah. Sonny Cohn replaces him. Because he walked off the band stand from that thing, and don‘t know where he went. He left the band just like that. Then they got Sonny Cohn. Sonny lived out in Chicago I think it was. Wasn‘t Sonny from Chicago?
I don‘t know, I‘m asking you. [laughs] There‘s not a lot about a lot of these guys, like you know Al…
Yeah, he was from Chicago.
Okay, Sonny Cohn.
And they got Sonny Cohn and then Al Aarons, who did he replace?
